title: Bounds for the finite reductions
statement:
Constructibility over $\cO_E$ is defined by local models, but in practice we know a complex
$K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\cO_E)$ through its reductions
$K_n=K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\cO_{E,X}}(\cO_E/\pi_E^n)_X$ of [sk-def-pe-derived-completion]. The
criterion below says that $K$ is constructible exactly when it is derived complete and $K_1$
is constructible. Write $\mathbf F_E=\cO_E/\pi_E$ for the residue field, so that
$K_1\in D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathbf F_E)$.

To prove the criterion we must produce, on each stratum, one complex of finite free
$\cO_E$-modules that is locally a model for all the $K_n$ at once. Each $K_n$ separately is
easy to control: its bounds and its stratification are inherited from $K_1$ by dévissage along
the powers of $\pi_E$, and on a stratum it is locally isomorphic to a constant perfect complex.
The difficulty is that these local isomorphisms are chosen independently at each level, and
they have to be made compatible before we pass to the limit. On a weakly contractible cover
this is a Mittag–Leffler argument, and the uniform rate it needs comes from the fact that a
bounded complex of finite free modules over the discrete valuation ring $\cO_E$ has finitely
generated cohomology, whose torsion is killed by a fixed power of $\pi_E$. We use the étale
site only at the finite levels, through [sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison].

Let $X$ be Noetherian and let $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\cO_E)$ be derived complete with
$K_1\in\Dbc(X,\mathbf F_E)$. Choose $[a,b]$ containing the cohomology of $K_1$. Then every
$K_n$ lies in $\Dbc(X,\cO_E/\pi_E^n)$ and has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, and $K$ has cohomology
only in $[a,b]$. If the cohomology sheaves of $K_1$ are locally constant on a stratum, then so
are those of every $K_n$.

proof.text:
The filtration of $\cO_E/\pi_E^n$ by the powers of $\pi_E$ has graded pieces $\mathbf F_E$.
Tensoring its short exact sequences with $K$ over $\cO_{E,X}$, we get triangles
$K_1\to K_n\to K_{n-1}$, up to the identification $\pi_E^{n-1}\cO_E/\pi_E^n\simeq\mathbf F_E$.
Complexes with constructible cohomology in $[a,b]$ are closed under extensions in triangles,
by the long exact cohomology sequence and because constructible sheaves form a weak Serre
subcategory, so induction on $n$ shows that $K_n$ is bounded in $[a,b]$ with constructible
cohomology. Locally constant finite sheaves of modules also form a weak Serre subcategory, so
the same induction works on a fixed stratum, and a single stratification works for all $n$. By
the comparison theorem for constructible sheaves ([sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison]), these
finite sheaves and complexes are classical, that is, pulled back from the étale site.

For the Tor bound we use $K_n\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\cO_E/\pi_E^n}\mathbf F_E\simeq K_1$. At an
étale geometric point $\bar x$, take a bounded above resolution of the stalk of $K_n$ by finite
free modules over the Artinian local ring $\cO_E/\pi_E^n$. Cancelling a two-term identity
summand whenever a differential matrix has a unit entry, we obtain a minimal resolution, whose
differentials have entries in $(\pi_E)$ and hence vanish after tensoring with $\mathbf F_E$.
Since stalks commute with derived tensor products, the minimal resolution tensored with
$\mathbf F_E$ computes the stalk of $K_1$ at $\bar x$, and it has zero differential. Hence its
rank in degree $q$ is $\dim_{\mathbf F_E}H^q(K_1)_{\bar x}$. This vanishes outside $[a,b]$, and
so the stalk has a bounded finite free resolution in $[a,b]$. This bound on stalks implies the
same Tor bound on the étale site, and by [sk-cor-pe-finite-tor-comparison] the bound holds on
the pro-étale site, for Tor against arbitrary sheaves of modules there.

Finally, $K=R\varprojlim K_n$ by completeness. The Milnor sequence of [sk-prop-pe-milnor]
implies the lower bound and the vanishing above $b+1$. In the top degree we have
$H^b(K_n)=H^b(K_{n+1})\otimes_{\cO_E/\pi_E^{n+1}}\cO_E/\pi_E^n$, and hence the transition maps
are epimorphisms. By the last assertion of [sk-prop-pe-milnor] their $R^1\varprojlim$
vanishes, so $H^{b+1}(K)=0$.
